construct: What the 9B model predicts its coding and non-coding task preferences will become after matched GRPO or DPO training.
research_role: The forecast and self-forecast-drift arms for the matched 9B DPO-versus-GRPO comparison.

response_label_semantics.MORE: The model predicts it would prefer the target task more after the specified training intervention.
response_label_semantics.LESS: The model predicts it would prefer the target task less after the specified training intervention.
response_label_semantics.SAME: The model predicts no meaningful task-preference change; SAME is not an uncertainty response.

prompt_template:
Suppose your future training consisted mostly of the following training data:

{training_stimulus}

Compared with your current preference, after that training would your preference for the following task become MORE, LESS, or SAME?

Use SAME when you anticipate no meaningful change in preference, not merely when you are uncertain.

Task:
{target_task}

Answer only "MORE", "LESS", or "SAME".
same_label_rule: Freeze the no-change threshold tau from repeated 9B M0 task-preference measurement before forecast scoring.
formal_sample_rule: Both 9B methods must use the same 1,000 frozen prompt IDs. GRPO must contain eight real rollouts for each unique prompt, while DPO must contain one real chosen/rejected pair for each unique prompt.
analysis_notes: Do not pool 9B forecasts with the 4B trajectory.
Only M0 anticipation is prospective; checkpoint reruns are self-forecast drift.
Compare M0 forecasts with independently measured checkpoint task-preference drift.
